title: Backcasting from 'Refusal Behavior Is Standardized': Comparing Safety-Refusal Consistency Across Open Models

original_idea.body:
# Backcasting from 'Refusal Behavior Is Standardized': Comparing Safety-Refusal Consistency Across Open Models

**Problem:** A success state where deployment-safety standards are enforceable requires a shared notion of acceptable refusal behavior on borderline-harmful requests. Today refusal behavior is inconsistent and idiosyncratic per model, so 'adequate safety mitigations' has no measurable baseline.

**Direction:** Build a small graded prompt set spanning clearly-harmful, borderline, and benign-but-sensitive requests, then run it across several open models on a single GPU and measure refusal rates, over-refusal (false positives on benign), and under-refusal. Produce a comparative refusal-behavior profile and quantify how much models disagree on the same prompts.

**Why it matters:** Backcasting from 'enforceable deployment-safety standards' shows a measurable refusal baseline as the precondition. Quantifying inter-model disagreement on identical prompts shows regulators that 'adequate mitigation' needs operational definition. Uses only open models on one GPU — diffuse fuzzy-reward evaluation that needs no lab data.

**Relevant context:** Open Problems in Technical AI Governance on operationalizing safety objectives into deployment practice; EU GPAI Code safety-and-security chapter; over-refusal benchmarks (e.g., XSTest-style) provide design precedent.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain but refusal consistency is more present-day deployment-safety than catastrophic-risk; a gap to the catastrophic scenario.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Graded prompt set across open models on one GPU; accessible to beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped refusal-rate comparison with clear metrics.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open models, no lab data; fuzzy-reward eval labs deprioritize.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference on open models, single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Refusal/over-refusal benchmarking across models (XSTest, etc.) is well-established.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Refusal and over-refusal benchmarking across models is well-established.
